t2i_prompt: A 1440 px wide desktop web section as a flat straight-on UI mockup in Swiss International Typographic Style on warm limestone. A very large light-weight sans headline in sentence case across the top, a thin breadcrumb bar above it. Below, slash-numbered uppercase column headers and a strict grid of rows; each row opens with a solid deep navy tile holding a huge light white numeral with slash, then limestone cells with hairline borders, a small label above a larger value, the last column in monospace, for <CONTENT>. One or two cells hold a small white pipe-and-valve blueprint on steel blue. Square corners, flat, no shadows.
signature_idea: A verification table whose rows are anchored by a spine of navy slash-numeral tiles, so a plain router reads like a Swiss poster.
strengths: navy numeral spine makes five routes instantly scannable
label-over-value cells keep each column's meaning explicit
palette, light headline, mono times and square corners are on-brand
maps directly to a token-only CSS grid table
weaknesses: essentially a table on a frame; blueprint tiles are decoration that mean nothing for the row
repeated cell labels duplicate the column headers
duplicated word in one cell ('the the') and invented location and dates
one stray white cell breaks the palette rhythm
brand_fit_why: Navy and limestone tiles, light headline, mono figures and square corners match the brand, but it is close to a plain table with decorative blueprint insets.
